post.description: *Try* on a draft indicator: the server evaluates the posted (unsaved) Measure over the package version's test patients (`tests/` files of type `test-patient`) for a period type and period as a Report would choose them, on the FHIRPath engine every node runs. Each record of the Measure's basis is placed in the period by its period date (up to its end, cumulative), and the criteria decide whether it counts; people and enrollments count once each, visits and observations each one. A percentage, rate or ratio's numerator is within its denominator; a sum, average, median, minimum, maximum or distinct count takes each counted thing's first or last value. Criteria may compare dates with `%periodStart` and `%periodEnd` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and `%previousPeriods.start` (the starts of the periods before, the nearest first), and may require a patient to be in another indicator of the package's numerator or denominator (`'<url>|<version>' in %indicators.numerator`), which is evaluated first. It answers the figure with what roll-up needs and every test patient with each record's part, so the editor shows who is counted and why.

post.description: The Workflow Studio's sandbox: plays the posted (unsaved) draft Workflow Definition in the engine's simulation with every action stubbed, from the start through each move (an event or an ISO 8601 wait), with the author's guard answers and gate outcomes. It answers what held after each move: the configuration, the stubbed actions, the pending timers, the open Tasks and the events the configuration accepts. A move that would evaluate an unanswered guard is not taken and the guards are reported, never guessed. The run comes back as a `workflow-scenario` file for *Save as scenario*.

post.summary: Documents and takes one lifecycle step.
post.description: Takes one lifecycle step as the signed-in account, checked again here whatever the list said: the permission, the stage, the Draft Holder and the separation of duties. `request-changes` needs a `reason`, `activate` a `scope` (`national`, `district:<code>`, `facility:<code>` or `program:<facility>:<program>`). `check` (*Check now*) runs validation and simulation on a draft and keeps the results, leaving it in Draft. `hand-over` offers the draft `to` a username, who holds it once they `accept-handover`; `decline-handover` calls the offer off. `reassign` (`metadata.manage`) gives it `to` a username at once, for a `reason`. `withdraw` ends an unpublished draft and keeps it under another id, freeing its `name@version`. Answers the page as it is afterwards, under the id it is kept as.
